title: Flood Re Explained: Affordable Flood Cover for UK Homes
description: How Flood Re helps UK homes in flood-risk areas get affordable insurance, which homes are eligible, why post-2009 homes are excluded and the 2039 end.
intro: If you live somewhere at high flood risk in the UK, you may have benefited from Flood Re without knowing it. Here’s how the scheme works and whether your home qualifies.

image.alt: Floodwater surrounding stone buildings and a partly submerged car

blocks.title: Key points
rows: A reinsurance scheme run jointly by government and insurers.
Through your normal home insurer; you can’t buy from Flood Re directly.
Homes built before 1 January 2009 can be eligible.

sections.html: Insurers can pass (“cede”) the flood part of an eligible home policy to Flood Re for a set price based on the home’s council tax band. That lets them offer cover at prices they might not otherwise. All UK home insurers pay a levy that funds the scheme.

Broadly, a home must be residential, in council tax bands A–H (or equivalent), insured by the occupants or left empty, and built before 1 January 2009. Some types of property and policy, including certain landlord, leasehold block and commercial arrangements, aren’t eligible. Flood Re’s own website has an eligibility checker and a list of insurers using the scheme.

Excluding newer homes is meant to discourage building in flood-prone areas without proper protection. Flood Re is designed as a transition: by 2039 the aim is for flood insurance to be affordable through a combination of better flood defences, resilient homes and risk-reflective pricing. That’s why Flood Re also promotes property flood resilience, such as through “Build Back Better” payments some insurers offer after a flood.

faqs.q: Do I need to apply to Flood Re?
faqs.a: No. Buy home insurance as usual; if your insurer uses Flood Re and your home is eligible, it can use the scheme behind the scenes.
No. It’s for eligible households only.
